transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you lately and what brings you into the clinic today?

I've been feeling really depressed and sad almost constantly, and it has been going on for over two years now. I just can't seem to shake this heavy, low mood, which is why I decided to finally come in today.

During these past two years, have there been any periods of at least two weeks where your mood was significantly worse, accompanied by symptoms like loss of interest, fatigue, or changes in sleep and appetite?

It hasn't really been in isolated two-week blocks; instead, this low mood, constant fatigue, and changes in my appetite have been mostly continuous for the last two years and one month. I've felt this heavy sadness and exhaustion almost every single day without much of a break.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a continuous low mood lasting over two years without significant symptom-free intervals, which strongly aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia). Given the lack of distinct, episodic major depressive episodes mentioned, Major Depressive Disorder is less likely as a primary diagnosis.
